episodes.title: The SEMA Show has changed over the years…
Conor Shanahan

moments.quote: there's no way that you could tell me that 2018 James Dean would absolutely destroy 2026. James, it's not possible. Yeah. And that's what I think a lot of people look up to James for is that like, he came back and like James is drifting quite a long time now and he's came. He's from, if you were to go back 12, 13 years ago and take a driver who retired and, and say, come back to drifting now. They wouldn't, I personally believe that they would struggle massively, but how much the sport has changed. I think Digo Saito is a great example that like,
moments.why: Gekozen door Joshua op het dashboard

moments.topic: THE TROPHY FLEW HOME IN A DRINKS CABINET
moments.quote: I got to ask about the logistics of bringing that trophy home. Like, did you end up booking a separate seat or like, did you have to keep it on your lap for the whole time or how did that all work out? Yeah, it was quite funny. Actually, the airline that we fly with to California is an Irish airline, Erlingus. Erlingus, yeah. So they're like really supportive, quite cool to, you know, ...
moments.why: Light, funny story about flying the 2026 FD trophy home to Ireland. Easy share.

moments.quote: To bring it home is always quite special. And yeah, I think I'm kind of a guy who like loves the small moments, you know, like it's always nice to come home and, you know, put it on the kitchen table for the first time. And I think when my mom will not take it off the kitchen table for at least probably two months. So that's kind of the rule. If we have a big win, they stay down there. ...
moments.why: Sweet family detail: big wins stay on the kitchen table for two months.

moments.topic: ONE HAND ON THE TITLE, NOT BOTH
moments.quote: Yeah, I'm also a big believer in that it's not over until it's in my hand, you know, and that's kind of yeah, I guess the break between Vegas and Long Beach was quite rough because it's I have one hand on it, but not both. You know, it's very close to being done and but still anything going to happen. I think that's what added so much pressure to the battle. Everyone's like, oh, it's just a top pretty too. But I'm like, yeah, but if I lose this top, or two, Jack or James going to win the event. So I'm not going to be champion.
moments.why: How the pressure felt between Vegas and Long Beach; fans remember that final.

moments.topic: "HE WAS GOING TO BE AN FD CHAMPION"
moments.quote: we all know that here, but I was going to be an FT champion, right? Like, yeah, I think, I think that's a foregone conclusion to be honest. Yeah. So I think like it's in Jerry's point of view, like he worked hard with that kid, the hero worked hard and I felt like he was maybe the last shot was took away from a little bit. So I'm like happy that, you know, you know, hero is such a good ...
moments.why: Conor zegt dat Hiroya Minowa een zekere toekomstige FD-kampioen was voordat hij naar rally ging.

moments.topic: COULD HIROYA MINOWA RACE A US RALLY?
moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. It's, it's tough to see him step away into rally. And, but at the same time, like it looks like he's doing well there. I have a very strong feeling. We're going to see him climb the ranks of, of rally very soon, which might be very, which could be cool. Cause they're going to have around in the U S next year. So like the chance, there is a chance we might be able to see him ...
moments.why: Speculatie dat Hiroya Minowa volgend jaar een Amerikaanse rallyronde rijdt. Gerucht, gaat naar Joshua.

moments.topic: "YOU DRIVE HOW THE JUDGES TELL YOU"
moments.quote: you know, like, you know, the argument of people saying, Oh, you can't drive how you want to drive in competition. Well, no shit, you know, like, yeah, yeah, exactly. You know, you're going to drive. Yeah, I don't really understand that point. But yeah, of course, like we all critique stuff. We all maybe want stuff to be a little bit different. I think, you know, drifting is involving as a whole when it comes to our rule book and a judging rule book. But I don't get that sometimes, you know, I don't get that point of like, Oh, like, you know, competition driving, you don't drive how you want to drive. But like, that's kind of the whole point, right? Like you go to a room in the morning tree, guys tell you what to do. And you do that job the best you can, and you're going to win the you know, that's kind of my opinion how it works.
moments.why: Strong opinion on the 'you can't drive how you want' debate. Comment bait.

moments.quote: You need real people around you. You don't need people around you that are telling you like, Oh, well you've done good. You know, you lost the battle, but you almost had them. Like that's the part for me. When somebody says to me, I almost had you. I'm like, but you didn't. Yeah. That's the difference. Yeah. Almost had like, I would never, I hate that work being honest. There's one thing what annoys me in drifting when somebody says, Oh, but we almost had you, but you didn't. Yeah. You weren't good enough to have me. So go back and be realistic about that.
moments.why: Blunt quote, very shareable.

moments.topic: HIS SPOTTER WATCHES DRIFT EVENTS IN EGYPT
moments.quote: I said at the banquet, like, I would often text him late at night. And I'm like, what are you doing? He's like, I'm just watching a drift event. And I'm like, where's the drift event? And it's in like Egypt or something. And I'm like, you know, and I love drifting also. And I always felt for a while that I would never meet somebody who loved drifting just as much as me. But I definitely ...
moments.why: Funny detail about how obsessed his spotter Matt is. Name spelling: check.

moments.quote: me and Matt have a very simple number system, what we use. So like in battle situations, like a lot of the time, so Matt will give me a rundown before the battle, what I'm warming the towers up, what to expect, what to approach. But after that, it's very, it's very simple communication. We have a number system that we've studied very to a very high level. You maybe will see me do ...
moments.why: He and his spotter use a number system; slow practice runs are them practising it.

moments.topic: "IF IT FAILS, MY AMERICAN JOURNEY IS OVER"
moments.quote: You know, I talked about a lot about this journey year that in first 15 minutes, I knew that we were going to fight for a championship. That's very true. Like, that's not a saying that I just came up with that actually happened. And it wasn't that the car was that good. I didn't even drive the car at this point. But jury and his team gave me a sense of like, this is where I meant to be ...
moments.why: Strongest story of the episode: all-in bet on Jerry Yang's team.

moments.topic: "JAMES BEATING US WAS THE BEST THING"
moments.quote: we're like, I think we can get back to a good position. Do I think that we can fight for championship? Maybe not. You know, for sure, it wasn't a perfect year. There was still some things what could have been better on my side. And, you know, we had a little bit of bad look. But like, overall, when I look back at the year, I think it was everything what it needed to be. James whooped ...
moments.why: Says losing to James Deane in Orlando turned the season.

moments.topic: HIS CREW CHIEF DOES THE TESTING
moments.quote: Eric, my crew guy, holy shit, he can drive. Like, I actually really want to drive with him. I have watched a lot of these videos and stuff. And like, so anytime the car needed to get tested when I wasn't there, Eric was the one who done the testing on my car as well. Which I thought was sick. Like, there's not many teams can say that their crew chief guy was the guy who was driving it ...
moments.why: Little-known fact: crew chief Eric tests the car when Conor is in Europe.

moments.topic: 1,500 WHP AND NO NOS ALL YEAR
moments.quote: Even in Europe, there was a long time that I used like a smaller turbo than Jack. Right. So the VR suits my style, but then the VR went to the other extreme where we had a problem that it just was too much. Like the engine was too much. Like I was constantly asking to turn it down, turn it down, turn it down, turn it down. To the point that we almost couldn't turn it down anymore. First ...
moments.why: Big numbers and a surprising choice: he asked to turn the engine DOWN.

moments.quote: I was always like, oh, there's a way that we can make run -up better. There has got to be a way to like chasing on the run -up has to be better. So I started left foot braking always on the run -up, on the chase. So I would left foot brake to flick, like mimic the speed. Um, if there, even in Poland and my onboards and stuff, like Dylan Hughes asked me in FD, he was like, that blows my ...
moments.why: Claims he started left-foot braking on the chase run-up and others copied it (mentions Dylan Hughes and LZ). Check names.

moments.quote: There is not much of an off season actually. Um, yeah, I go to Japan next week to do D1, which I'm excited about. Um, yeah, so I got to go there and then I will go to Cyprus, which is kind of like a traditional trip. What Irish drivers do at the end of the year. I haven't went actually in the last three years, so I'm excited to go there. Um, and then I do a rally, which is kind of like ...
moments.why: D1 in Japan, Cyprus, a rally and Oman. Note: recorded right after Long Beach, so 'next week' may be past.

moments.topic: WHY FD IS SO HARD TO WIN
moments.quote: Like no one just becomes a champion without working hard. Like F.D. is probably one of the hardest motorsport championships to win because like you can have the best team in road racing and be a decent driver and keep all four tires on the ground and win a championship road racing. Yeah, it is not like that drifting at all, because you can make a mistake every lap and still win road racing. Yeah, you cannot do that in drifting unless the other guy you're battling does it, too. Yeah. You almost can't make a mistake in a weekend. Like you got to go all the way. And like, you know, usually you make one or two and hopefully the other guy does, too. And then you got to beat the three guys up top that are deciding who wins. Right. Right. Understand what they want. Yeah. Because I'm not fighting for a lap time. Yeah. I'm fighting for a I win or lose.
moments.why: Road racing lets you make mistakes every lap; in drifting one mistake and judges decide.

moments.quote: Like it's like to me, it's very clear. Like I don't think there's to me, there's always a vast difference. Because I think the rules and how F.D. is currently, it doesn't like if you drive the whole track at 50 degrees angle and you fill every zone and then the next guy goes out and does it at 62 degrees angle and fills all the zone, does all the same thing, they're getting the same score. That's what I believe. The problem with F.D. is right now, because the guy with 50 degrees angle did everything great and he did everything he was supposed to. OK. Driving at 62 degrees angle versus 50 is five times harder. Right. Should be that other run should be a 65 and that's a 95.
moments.why: Same run at 62 degrees vs 50 gets the same score now; he says it should be 95 vs 65.

moments.quote: And I think it's just because like all those dudes, I've watched James and Connor and Vaughn and like all these guys go drive fun events. And you're like, these dudes are insane. Yeah, they shred. And then you go to F.D. and you're like, good chases, strong leads. I think there's an incentive for consistency. Sure. Right. Sure. But also like if your normal run got a 60 and qualifying. And everybody just did normal runs. The guy who drove hard and pushed the limits would blow everybody's doors off. But it's not even possible. Like, yeah, you could do a run that's unbelievable. And it's going to be three points better than the guy who hit all the zones and did everything. So do you I guess like with all that said, what's what is the fix? I mean, a normal run should be a 65. It's just barely passing.
moments.why: Top drivers shred at fun events but play it safe at FD because risk is not rewarded.

moments.quote: Oh, I know. So what like if I if they brought back qualifying like the way it is right now and everybody's in, I'm not fighting to like fill a spot. My crew would be so bummed. You I want more events qualifying 25th to 32 than qualifying up top. Qualifying poorly, like almost is better in the long run.

episodes.title: The rise of PERFORMANCE SEDANS… Are 4 doors better than 2?
Rafael Muller aggressive grassroots drifter from Switzerland

moments.quote: Being from Switzerland I found out at Tomodori that you guys do not have any race tracks and motorsports are completely illegal in the country. Well almost yeah like we don't have a race track and circuit racing was forbidden till now. Actually they changed the law this year. No way. Yeah so you could build a race track right now. What we have is like pretty cool hill climbs but like the hill climbs in Switzerland like nothing against them but it's like hard as a normal human you know like it's not easy access to be there. It's like the same old 50 drivers from like 30 years ago which like drive there. But other than that it's I would say yeah hard to do racing like even people who do like motocross they normally go to Italy or like we we go to like France for drifting
moments.why: Swiss drifter explains a country with no race tracks where circuit racing was banned until this year.

moments.quote: Yeah you need to do like a trailer license which is not I mean you just need to do it it's like a driver license but just for the trailer. Then he like back a trailer open stuff. Yeah yeah yeah I think I probably wouldn't have been able to get a trailer license for all. I mean yeah there is like if it's it's it's not hard it's just annoying to do because like you can get like a like a learning permit and you can drive for like two years and then you need to do like the exam and like I mean I drove around Europe with a trailer and like the exam you need to like it matters if you first you know like put the electric part on and then put the like the hitch it's called I feel. Yeah yeah yeah. You know like if you first do the hitch and then the electric part is already like oh no you know. You fail. Yeah you fail.
moments.why: Swiss drifters need a special trailer license, and the exam can be failed on the order of plugging in.

moments.quote: I met him one or two days after I did my driver license randomly on a parking lot he was like shooting pictures of his e36 and I just had my new e30s I was feeling pretty cool you know I had my driver license and shit and he was like oh cool car and I was like yeah tomorrow I install coilovers on it and he was like if you need a hand like let me know and I actually fucked something up like my brake line you know I yeah I just fucked it up and I needed his help and he came over and he was like yeah you say like yesterday that you really like drifting and stuff I'm also interested and I checked last night that there's like a drift event in France should we just like go there and I was like yeah sure like and we went drifting I had my license for like two weeks I mean I didn't knew nothing like I bought the ticket to go drift there and he asked me like do you have an LSD and I was like what is an LSD right he was like yeah let's you know like let's hit that roundabout and I had actually I was lucky I had like OEM LSD with the winter package you know like e36
moments.why: Origin story: two weeks after getting his license he drove seven hours to a French drift day without knowing what an LSD was.

moments.topic: SWISS COILOVERS: 30% MORE AND A TEST
moments.quote: so how it works like you you need to buy kwe like I explained you like imagine you you have a car here you want to install the same idea so you need to see who imports though that brand right so you see ah there's a shop he imports kwe and he will sell you the coilovers for I would say like 30 percent more than they will cost anywhere else because they paid a lot of money to like make them street legal so you buy it with like papers like like a confirmation like okay those coilovers they fit that car and you can drive them so you install them but that's not all after that you need to like go to the inspection center they put it on a lift and they check if you mounted everything right if the right height is good if nothing wraps they go drive the car if something wraps you're walking home you know
moments.why: How street-legal coilovers work in Switzerland: approved brand, import markup, inspection and a test drive.

moments.quote: the cops are like just driving around to search for modified cars wow yeah and that's like that's the hard point because uh what I wanted to say like other countries they maybe have similar rules but it's just like the risk to get caught is less or like a cop will stop you and will be like it's probably illegal but you know like just fucking drive home I give you a warning or whatever which here it's like extremely lucky to like have that yeah like yeah yeah like they're taking your car yeah and it's expensive yeah and you you even like I had a friend he had like basic drift car and he he still had plates on it but the last time he did the inspection was like two years ago and over that time he like did you know basically 36 like no interior anymore like was like swapped it for a 28 and was like 23 on the paper as well as everything he paid like over 10k and lost his license for like two years
moments.why: Swiss police actively hunt modified cars; a friend's drift car cost him over 10k and his license for two years.

moments.topic: A PRINCE IN THE POLAND PADDOCK
moments.quote: and you have cars from everywhere yeah there was a guy like just next to me in a paddock and he shipped his fucking um what was it bent lay full carbon body and he's like a prince of Abu Dhabi like Joel told me probably the richest person you will ever see in your life because you know who it was like yeah and next to it you have like polish guy pumping hard style and super low he's 36 so it's cool like it was a cool like a mixture of drifting we had everything
moments.why: At a huge Polish drift event a full carbon Bentley from Abu Dhabi royalty parked next to a slammed E36 blasting hardstyle.

moments.quote: when this car popped up like how often are there nicely done Silvias that are like legal street legal in Switzerland there are probably just three cars Jans, mine and there's a yellow one I would say who are like in that style street legal but that car I mean I seven years before I bought that car was like yeah almost a kid I texted that guy if you one day sell it let me know yeah and so he's like I'm ready yeah I mean he saved your number no I saw it I saw it for sale I was like I texted him and I sold the M3 I had and everything so sold everything just to buy that car I was like I need that
moments.why: His Silvia is one of only about three street-legal built Silvias in Switzerland, and he waited seven years to buy it.

moments.topic: WHY EURO DRIFT DAYS ARE WET
moments.quote: but the reason why is noise like yeah it's just like less noise and also um most tracks I mean if they have imagine they have like a drift day on dry and like three days afterwards they have like bike racing and it rains and with the rubber like you know like they can't drive so yeah that's why most tracks do like yeah okay we don't like drifting but if we do it we just do it like on wet
moments.why: Explains why so many European tracks only allow drifting on a sprayed wet surface.

moments.quote: the compact also I have it now for like 10 years and the car is fucked like everything is fucked like yeah I have a rule to not spend more than one hour before going drive it like I do a timer the one hour passes I just go as it is and that's the rule it just keeps running I mean it's but is it a 323 ti is it a m42 no it's a m52 oh it swaps no it's original compacts they had six cylinders in here really yeah of course m52 baby
moments.why: His beat-up BMW compact runs on a strict rule: one hour of work max, then it goes on track as is.

moments.quote: it was getting to a point where I where I started not to like it anymore because it felt like a lot of drivers were more driving like demolition derby you know like just get drunk and fucking crash into each other all like they bought like a I don't know like a Volvo for like 200 bucks and they went there drink beers the whole day and just like crashed into each other's and I started to not like that that much but some years after it started to be like people who really drive good like good drivers who drive comp and everything and they were like let's just everyone gets really simple really cheap car we set them up like super grippy with good tires and we just like try to drive as hard as we can without like still driving good you know clean like not crashing for fun into each other and that made it like I had so fucking cool laps there like amazing laps and you're just like you doesn't care like you yeah just like the car is if you know if you total it no one cares that you still don't try to total it
moments.why: A lawless French wet drift event went from drunk demolition derby to good drivers pushing cheap grippy cars.

moments.quote: I did it once like back with the e36 there was like uh was called king of europe and they did like yeah they did like an amateur that's when I started they did like an amateur thing and I was like so hyped you know I was like buying brand new tires with my last money I was like yeah sick and I was not really good but I was not also really bad in that comp right but I felt like man I paid so much to be here and I'm not driving much like this is not fun also the pressure was not really my thing like there I love like the the comp thing about like I want to you know like for me there is nothing cooler that than have people on track who drive way better than I do because that hypes up to like you know like okay cool you know I want to try the same and get better and everyone has like different goals what someone to get more angles someone wants more smoke someone wants to come faster whatever you know like but just like keep pushing to somehow get better for what you love that's important for me otherwise it will get pretty boring
moments.why: A grassroots driver explains why one amateur comp was enough and what really pushes him to get better.

moments.quote: the other thing that I the advice like I don't know where this came from but it was like a way to deal with stress in the moment is think about yourself at like 90 years old yeah that's a good one and how you would feel about getting to relive that moment and try and live that moment from that perspective that's beautiful yeah yeah I don't know because like the desire of being 90 years old and like how much you would romanticize like the shot at getting to like be at a drift event with all your friends and driving again you know like yeah and just know that some point you're gonna be there and like why not enjoy it in that same way
moments.why: Palmer shares a simple mindset trick for enjoying stressful drift days.

moments.quote: they like they don't let you go very fast I don't think you'd enjoy it okay you can drive it it's like it's like a hundred bucks for like a certain amount of laps but like I also I tried to rent it one time and they're like fuck off like you know you're not driving our car I was like what do you mean and they're like no okay but like I think they thought I was gonna because they're like don't go to third is like one of the rules oh really yeah yeah so what's the point that's what I'm saying I was like okay they're like you can't go to third and I was like well then I'm not doing it yeah oh okay no so yeah I mean yeah it'll be fun but you're not going to be able to do the entry I think it but that will be the fun part that's the whole point of the track
moments.why: Palmer on renting a drift car at Ebisu: they told him to get lost, and the rule is no third gear.

moments.quote: I'm really honest I miss to be in a team I love that energy like Dom and kinfe with the s14 we lived in the same apartment for two and a half years and we were just drifting like our apartment was full of tires and spare parts and we had like our living room was just like tree sim rigs so yeah it was like we just lived for that we were like there is just drifting in our life so you really like streeting or like playing sim like yeah like just like and also never no one went somewhere to pick some parts up there was always oh yeah I'm coming I'm coming with you on a Tuesday night we arrived like one in the morning that was not a question you want to come with me it was just like oh yeah let's go you know that was cool we were young
moments.why: Nostalgic story of living with teammates in an apartment full of tires, spare parts and sim rigs.

moments.quote: the most important is like don't push yourself for something that you don't really want for yourself like I'm not talking about having like blowing an engine and that's again like taking the finger out of the asshole and just like okay you need to go through that you'll still love it but like if you feel like to be honest it doesn't give me the same as it used to you don't need to like force yours I see a lot of people I'm like I feel they're done with drifting but they're just doing it because they have nothing else or too much it's become they're like yeah I don't know too much of their identity like yeah yeah personality to be honest I also will have the same like I don't really have that many friends out of drifting stuff like if drifting will be away now will be a pretty empty life
moments.why: Honest take on people who keep drifting out of identity, and admitting his own life would be empty without it.

moments.quote: try not to be hard on people for changing because you don't know what you're gonna be into in front of years because like yeah that's why I was the kid on the internet talking hell of shit about anybody whose car wasn't low yeah and like same calling them a fucking oh you know what I have to you want to be you blah blah blah you know whatever you know what I like now this day today I'm just like fuck what height your car is like I know I was at the I was once the guy was like style over performance you know like if you will like do that interview eight years ago I would say style over performance but now I'm at the point like whatever you know like just having a really good balance yeah yeah yeah it is like it drives really fucking good but also looks really fucking good
moments.why: Both admit they used to roast anyone whose car was not low, and how their view changed.

moments.quote: so my car broke down um I I mean I met Carlos like once quick I think and I text him like dude are you not living near Barcelona I just my car broke down two in the morning was cold that was even was even illegal for me to drive to fucking Spain but I was like fuck it you know yeah um so yeah I texted him and I ended up being there stuck for like two weeks till I got the parts man I had two greats it's one of the greatest two weeks of my life like we went street drifting we drunk beers we're to like a car auction like he he was that time he was like yeah like doing like he's doing like car selling buying stuff it was so good and we ended up to be like really good friends
moments.why: His Land Cruiser died in Spain at 2am and a drifter he barely knew turned it into two of the best weeks of his life.

moments.quote: but imagine you're actually like living here and you go to Spain to drifting and you can't fucking talk to someone there yeah it's like everyone acts like it's okay but I think like it sucks you know it's really fucking sucks it's kind of no one will take out their phone and you know like you know like fucking translate the whole you're just like that's like normal yeah and they stay in their group and we stay in our group and we still have fun you know we laugh you know like you can show emotions but that deep connection is it's hard to get because I think like imagine whole Europe will speak like the same fucking language I think drifting will be on a other point that it is now will be like way more and way more connected and way like we will have something like final about I'm sure because there is a lot of cool shit here just like why not start it's a lot of pressure yeah I yeah I dreamed I think about that yeah I think it's possible
moments.why: Argues that the language barrier keeps European drifting apart, and one language would give Europe its own Final Bout.

moments.quote: who's the French dude with the blue uh s13 mike solvie like yeah he doesn't live that far like he lives not that far from the Swiss border dude that guy ritz and he's like you know so cool but he's like an og yeah he came to super team yeah yeah he was at semashow before yeah and he's like um yeah he drifted comp before with that car like was different of course like with sponsors and shit yeah and yeah I think he drifts for like over 20 years like he's really fucking og of France like he drifts for forever
moments.why: Shout out to an under-the-radar French OG in a blue S13 who has drifted for over 20 years without social media.

moments.quote: and it's so funny like doesn't really matter on like which level of well or like just having money you are like people always spend like everything they have so you have someone with like a hundred k car and he's in the same that someone with a 10k car they are doing the same you know like there's a percentage of income is going yeah it's one has like a 2025 truck with a brand new closed trailer and like a fucking crazy drift car running just like 265s and change them all second lap even if then they have tread on and you have someone who's like but they're doing the same they're like fuck yeah that's cool I never thought about it like that but that's so true yeah yeah just like for the love if you fucking love drifting like yeah you just it's you're spending 50 percent of your income on drifting yeah if not more
moments.why: Whether it's a 100k build or a 10k car, every drifter spends everything they have.

moments.topic: THE NIGHT AT THE JUDGES' TABLE
moments.quote: Final bout like believed in me to be like do you want to be a judge do you want to announce yeah I was like announce I don't think I'd be good at that and they're like I don't know you have a podcast like maybe you could figure it out first year I also not good was the first year the one you did with like I'm sorry I don't know his name the bold guy also really tall guy oh Jimmy Yates yeah yeah yeah but like a r32 yeah skyline yeah you did was that the first year that wasn't the first year okay but I was there when you did that that was fun when was it the year when like front sheet and proceed were going back to back yeah I'm like that was good that was a good year yeah that was really fun and me and Jimmy Yates were like you know and I mean like Raf and me that was the first year we went there mm -hmm and Raf and me we could like I don't know how we ended up there but we were like sitting on the judge table the whole night no and no one kicked us out like everyone was like yeah that was sick that was cool that was really cool that was a cool experience
moments.why: Palmer on becoming a Final Bout announcer, and Rafael sitting at the judges' table all night without being kicked out.

moments.topic: SWISS GUY VS AMERICAN BEER LAWS
moments.quote: I was filming at the entrance with a beer in my hand and the cops showed up and like 10 people were yelling at me like don't drink the beer don't drink the beer and I was like at the door of the cop with my beer and he was like are you the organizer of that event I was like oh no I'm not and they were like put the beer away put the beer away so I was like it's not okay that really happened like that's like a truth so yeah then we anyways I was saying that because like Chicago and it's like Illinois right and uh shawano is like Wisconsin and funny was like we went to like a camping you know like a RV fucking camp place at the lake in shawano and I bought some beers and I asked the lady there like do you have some covers for the beers because everyone told me you need those right and I was like yeah I'm in the US you know like I want to you know I adapt to where I am and she looked at me like what the fuck you want I was like yeah I need to cover the beer and that's three hours from fucking Chicago that's like the next state and she told me like I explained her like yeah I need to cover the beer and then she was like I never heard about that that you need to do that in the US just get your beer
moments.why: A Swiss drifter's confusion about US open container rules, from cops at Final Bout to a Wisconsin campsite.

moments.topic: A JOKE THAT BECAME FINAL BOUT
moments.quote: what would push you to like buy the ticket and go so I was not really doing well right and Raph called me like he was like oh yeah I want to do like a solo trip I was really like not doing well I was like I just need to like leave for a bit and go somewhere else and whatever had some vacations and then he was like just doing as a joke we could go to final bow and I was like I don't know man and then like I called him the next day I was like like you mean serious and he was like yeah it was like two weeks before final bow then we waited like one more week just talking about it and we were like okay let's do it you know and then we bought tickets and we were like oh we need a nesta that's like the document you need to like to come to the US so it was really spontaneous yeah just was like a fuck it let's do it thing yeah and yeah he was like struggling to like afford it and I think like his dad landed him some money he was like you know what like you're in your mid -20s you should experience that once I give you some money you pay me back and shit
moments.why: A rough year, a joke phone call and two weeks later two Europeans were on their way to Final Bout.

moments.quote: that's why the environment's important that's why I like going to people because it's like this is your space you know you can like tell your story in your space you know feels like therapy yeah a little bit that's my goal yeah I've actually been thinking about like going to school to be a therapist lately really yeah actually haven't said that brand new infos yeah we'll see I don't have a lot of but I think I care a lot about that I'm like helping people
moments.why: The Goodest Cast host drops brand new info: he's thinking about studying to become a therapist.

moments.guest: JAMES DEANE, JACK SHANAHAN, ADAM LZ
moments.quote: Especially when the sun goes down, we don't get any practice. Usually our qualifying laps are the first time we drive in a dark and all your reference points change. But I feel like FD did a really good job here in Long Beach too to light the track in the correct areas. It's the first time all year by the way. Yeah, so you're getting better. Yeah, so improvement. Remember what you did and do it again. I was a bit worried on the last corner because the smoke was such an issue before that. I was like, oh at night it's going to be terrible. moments.topic: OFF-SEASON: NORWAY, ICE AND NEW WIRING
moments.quote: I'm, uh, like last year, I don't know if you, if you know, if you knew, but I went to Norway for, uh, ice drifting and it was really, really fun. Um, very cool. So I definitely want to try to go back again because, uh, that was, uh, that was a fun experience. And for sure, I'm going to also set up my three fifties that I have at home for ice drifting. So it's going to be mainly the, uh, the, the big project for the, uh, for the drifting and the off season. And also we had a, uh, not a big fire, but a considerate, uh, good fire during the DMCC round, uh, back in Quebec here. So, uh, yeah, I think it would be wise to just put in a fresh, uh, set of wiring on the, on the car.
moments.why: Off-season plans: Norway ice drifting again and new wiring after a fire at a DMCC round.

moments.topic: WHY THE CORVETTE MAKES TINY MISTAKES LOOK BIG
moments.quote: I'm always comparing it with the S chassis, but I'm not trying to make the car drive like the S chassis because I know this car is way more sensitive, uh, or we can see twitchy, but also has a ton of front grip, which the S chassis was always lacking of. So like, I definitely don't want the Corvette to handle like the S S C. I just want to reduce the, uh, the, the, the things that are looking bad with the Corvette, which is always a small correction. They look so big because everything looks like everything looks more with the Corvette. So if you do something very good, it's going to look very good. Also, if you do a very tiny correction, it's also going to look big. And that's the main thing I'm focusing on to, uh, to get rid of for sure.
moments.why: Corvette has more front grip than his old S chassis but every small correction looks huge.

moments.topic: HIS ORANGE DEMO CAR IS 700 LBS HEAVIER
moments.quote: let me go back to my practice car, you know, my demo car that I brought at the world tour, which is now orange. Well, this car doesn't drive at all like my competition car. And some people that are not very deep into a drifting, sometimes they think it's the same car, you know, they're like, Oh, you brought your racing car or you change your living room, your car. Like, no, no, it's different. And it's like, you know, it's like a Miura and a, a, a Sauer. It's like two completely different car cause one, one, uh, weighs 2900 pounds. And the other one, the practice car weighs 3 ,600 pounds. So right there, there's a huge difference. And the weight distribution is like 5% different front to rear with the competition car. So all of that makes the car handles really, really differently.
moments.why: Fans think his orange demo car is his FD car. It is 3,600 lb versus 2,900 lb for the competition car.

moments.topic: GREY WHEELS AND BLACK GLOVES HIDE CORRECTIONS
moments.quote: Well, this, I made a decision, uh, quite some time ago to go with everything that's going to help me, uh, more than something that that's going to be more stylish. Back in the days, I, I was more like, okay, let's go white whales. Let's go with this and that, but being in pro, I feel that every little things that can help, help me, I will use it for me. So now I'm, uh, not black wheels, but it's a gray wheels. So you don't really see lots of the correction. Well, you see less correction than with white wheels for sure. Same things for my gloves. My gloves. Now I'm only using black gloves back in prospect when I won a championship in 24, I like a fluoro or a yellow gloves, which is like, you know, it's, it's cool. It's nice legs, but maybe not the wise, wise, the smooth to do when you want to, uh, you know, go under the radar with your correction.
moments.why: He switched from white wheels and fluo gloves to grey wheels and black gloves so judges see less correction.

moments.topic: C7 VS C6: NOT JUST A RESHELL

I thought it was like kind of just a re shelled. Hey, here's a, an updated look. Yeah. And I see that's what I thought at first. And I got into it and you're like, Oh, no, exactly. Like just said, told me when I started the project, he was like, you should just build a C six and put a C seven buddy kit on it. And it was like, hell no, I don't want to do this, but now I'm thinking about it. I'm like, maybe that would have been a good idea. You know, like a C six point five. Yeah. I like that. I like that. But, um, yeah, there is some difference, but also the whole chassis is aluminum. The subframes on aluminum, which is not the same in the, the C six platform. So it looks the same, but it is quite different. And then the rigidity, the rigidity of the chassis is like 30% more than the C six.
moments.why: The C7 chassis is aluminium with aluminium subframes and about 30 percent stiffer than the C6.

moments.quote: this, this season, I'm not going to drink a single beer just to know, to, you know, get more serious, be more focused or whatever. And it didn't really work. moments.quote: and I feel like at times it does get a little bit lazy with OEM plus stuff, because it's like, it's sort of like this proven formula that you know, will work if you've got, you know, a white 96 Civic and you're putting a bunch of Type R stuff on it from, you know, from the, from the UK nine. You already know what it's going to look like, right? Because there's a ton of them out there or you're putting the same exact parts that the other 30 guys in the next town over have on their white 96 Civic. I understand the appeal because it looks really, really good, but it's been done so many times before there's got to be a point where you're like, man, it's just, it's a clone, but there's so many that live exactly the same. So I do feel like at times that OEM plus stuff does get a little bit lazy. Um, but that's coming from someone that likes to modify. I like to tinker, I like to play with the car and change stuff up. So for me, if I was going to build something like that, it would be cool for a little bit, but then I'd have to, I have to do more of the plus side, like really start bringing in, uh, some market goods, cause I just get bored.
moments.why: Hot take that OEM+ builds are a copy-paste formula, sure to divide Honda fans.

moments.quote: I think the confusion is when you see a company like Nukem that's so closely related to Honda, a lot of people, especially the newer crowd, they think that those are actual Honda products. It's OEM stuff. It's not. It's an aftermarket brand, right? That company, especially, was so focused on motorsport products for so many years and they did so well. But in more recent years, you see a lot of that stuff they're making is just for like streetcars, right? So like floor mats and window visors. And I think they even have like a little protector that goes behind the door handle so your key doesn't scratch it. So there's all these little things they make, right? The little knickknacks and stuff. So you see them sort of transitioning, still making performance products, but also going into that realm as well. That stuff again, in my opinion, it's not OEM plus. That's aftermarket goods.
moments.why: Clears up a common myth: Mugen parts are aftermarket, not factory Honda.

moments.quote: Am I, on my VQ 37, I'm putting the GTR twin turbos on it because of, you know, fitment, it's the best setup I can do. But there's other companies that make great twin turbo kits that would be a much better option if it was in stock chassis and all that. But my point being like, there are way better aftermarket solutions than what the OE offers in that instance. So am I shooting myself in the foot and setting myself up to fail by saying, okay, I'm going to stay in this, you know, box and not do anything outside of it? Or do I just go for what's best and what's the best opportunity for me to build something? Yeah, I mean, it's your money, right? You have to decide what, how it's going to work for you, where you want to put it, because you don't get it back, right?
moments.why: Host reveals his VQ37 build uses GT-R twin turbos and questions sticking to OEM.

moments.topic: COLD AIR INTAKES DON'T MAKE POWER
moments.quote: And, you know, I've seen it firsthand cold air intakes and you know, as well as I do, do not make power. They're not, you know, putting a cold air intake does not necessarily mean that you're going to gain horsepower. You might gain a little bit of feel. It might move the power band around, depending on, you know, flow diameter of the pipe and things like that. Fine. But there's something to be said about a team of engineers that set out to make that, say that manifold, that exhaust manifold flow as efficiently as possible and to work as well as it does into obviously fit. They put a lot of time and effort into the fit and finish and how it's going to fit on the vehicle. And I think that's where we really see that shine through now.
moments.why: Bold claim against a classic first mod, backed by praise for factory engineering.

moments.quote: If not, wiring specialties just recently announced that they're doing a VR 30 swap kit for the Z33 chassis for the 350Z chassis. I think it is brilliant. Like genuinely, I think that it's very smart to keep the longevity of both of the platforms going. Like, yes, the VR 30 has its issues and everyone can complain. But yet again, a junkyard motor capable of 400 horsepower. Like, let's just, you know, lay that out there and going into a, you know, an O3, O4, 350Z platform, it's a super light chassis for that. And it's gonna and they're getting cheap. You know, let's be honest, the G35 and 350Z have come down significantly. So if you know, for one with a blown engine or anything like that, you can get a chassis. I'm saying for a decent price.
moments.why: Wiring Specialties VR30 swap kit for Z33: big news for budget drift chassis builders.

moments.quote: You know, I should say, it sounds like I'm sort of hating on OEM plus built. I'm definitely not. I did one for a little while. And like I said, you know, I got bored and I moved on. A little while. I didn't want a necessity at the time I was very young. And I may or may not have been charged for multiple counts of street racing and whatever. And then I had purchased a vehicle and I decided to put an engine in it. A lot of the vehicle stock, put a different Honda engine in it. Different OEM wheels and a lip from a higher model. I cruised that around for a while. And that was just what I had. And it was definitely OEM plus. And, you know, it worked for me, but eventually moved on.
moments.why: Funny confession: multiple street racing charges led to a quiet OEM+ Honda.

moments.quote: That ultimately led, especially in like the Honda and Nissan world, to a lot of theft. And I think it's, you know, it's pretty well known. Type Rs were constantly getting stolen. GSRs, you know, losing their engine transmission, wheels, brakes, seats, all that kind of stuff. So it definitely had a negative impact, but it was also a positive one because it got everybody modified and going nuts with building cars, you know. Especially we're talking, you know, like late 90s, early 2000s. I mean, it was insane how many people had built coming out. So, you know, there's the good and the bad, right? Because it definitely led to a lot more theft because people wanted to get those parts and they weren't willing to buy them. So there's a problem.
moments.why: How the hunt for higher-trim parts fuelled the late 90s Type R and GSR theft wave.

moments.quote: But even a junkyard cast iron 5 .3 liter can make 500 horsepower with the right setup in it. And you don't have that with a civic, let's say, like you're not, you're not going to be able to run out there and make a natural aspirated civic, make 500 horsepower. Like that's not a normal thing. And you're not going to probably be wanting to drive it once it is making 500 natural, natural aspirated horsepower. It's going to be quite a handful. I'm sure. So my, the thing that I think is that was always just the chase of how to make quick power, how to make it cheap. How to have a fast car. It was never about, hey, I need this part because it makes the car more like the higher trim level. You know, nobody was putting a Hellcat motor in their scat pack to make it a Hellcat. They were just doing it to have a fast scat pack.
moments.why: Domestic vs import: a junkyard LS makes 500 hp, a Civic never will.

moments.quote: That's the same thing with the Volkswagen crowd. And I think even the Corvette crowd too, right? Like the Corvette guys are like that way too, you know, that I don't, I don't know anything about high socks, new balances and tan shorts. I'm just saying they could all catch strays. It's okay. You know me, I have much more. I'll take my, my problems circled, you know, nice little Ford logo or the Nissan one. They circle my problems. I already know what I have. Don't worry.
moments.why: Lighthearted roast of Corvette owners, then a self-own about Ford and Nissan.

moments.quote: So for me, to see Audi parts on a Volkswagen is not uncommon. You know, to see, you know, S3 parts on a Jetta or what I don't know how it exactly works. But my point being to see those crossovers, not that big of a deal, where I start to have the issue is where it's like, oh, but for instance, we talked about it when we're talking about the OEM wheels. Check out that podcast if you haven't. I had Mustang wheels on my Nissan. To me, that's not OEM plus, even if it's a Mustang wheel off of a OEM car, because we've now switched genres, let's say, to me, or, you know, switch manufacturers, it's a completely no longer the case. It's always been that DNA, that continuation of the brand, makes it the OEM plus as in they've made the car better than what the manufacturer could by using the main or what the manufacturer could have made the car to be by using manufacturer parts. I guess is the way that I define it.
moments.why: A clear rule: OEM+ means parts from the same brand family, Mustang wheels on a Nissan don't count.

moments.topic: THE WING THAT BROKE THE INTERNET
moments.quote: On the outside of the car though, completely all Accord Euro R stuff, except for a big wing, because he didn't track the car once in a while, right? And then obviously aftermarket wheels. So in essence, I should not have been really called an OEM plus build. However, see to me, it's not. However, the rider, because he's just so smart, decided to call it an OEM plus build. And I mean, you call it a little bit of clickbait, I guess. But, you know, I basically kind of put in there that it was an OEM plus sort of build. And it caused - Plus plus build, OEM plus plus plus build. I think I actually said that in the end. But it's funny because it brought up a lot of commentary and it did its job as far as traffic, because people wanted to comment on it and say, you know, this or that. But it's funny because of all the posts that came up about it, like 95 % were all, how is OEM plus if it has that big wing in the back? Forget the brakes, the wheels, the suspension. All the bushing, all the stuff he did under, you know, all the stuff underneath, he had aftermarket seats, he had shifter, steering wheel, all the stuff, supercharged, it had her. The whole thing, right? So he had all the stuff done to it, but all anybody could focus on was the big wing.
moments.why: Story of an Acura TSX called OEM+ where commenters only cared about the wing.

episodes.title: Christian Cotrone

moments.topic: HIS HAPPY PLACE? OSW SKID PAD
moments.quote: Huge passion. I got to share with my dad growing up. Um, and to this day, man, like, uh, if you tell me like, where is your happy place, like I'm not going to tell you like a beach or a Bahamas, like I will tell you like the OSW skid pad, like it's just, you know, it's where I am comfortable is where I enjoy my time. And it's just being at the track, uh, the relationships we build out there as well. Um, I just, I love it, man.
moments.why: Cotrone picks a Florida skid pad over any beach, pure grassroots love.

moments.quote: yeah, I don't think I've missed the black Friday since I started driving. So this would probably be like my seventh or eighth year. Um, but it's been a while. It's I think I last time I won, it was in 21. There's definitely been a lot more changes, a lot more money involved now. But I don't know. It's like, I was talking to my wife about it, uh, about black Friday and she's like, you're not going to bring the Corvette. Are you? And I was like, ah, you know, there's, there's a lot of money on the line, but she's like, that's like, that's a lose lose. Because if you get the, you look like a dumbass, you're someone in their stock through DC and then if you win, they're just gonna go, Oh, you brought his pro car. You know, so it's, it's, I feel like it's very much so like a lose lose, but, uh, we'll see what we show up with.
moments.why: His wife calls bringing the FD Corvette to a grassroots event a lose-lose.

moments.quote: I was really, really fortunate for my first car. Uh, my uncle had like a few cars, a collection of cars, essentially. He was a big Camaro guy. Oh, so he had a replica SS 94 Z 28 Camaro and I had like 60 ,000 miles on it. And at that time it was probably, I don't know, 10, you know, like 10, 11 years old. So, you know, it had a low mileage and it just sat there. And so he basically was like, Hey, would you want to take this as your first car? It was in Pennsylvania. Um, and I just worked essentially for those two years straight to have enough money to get that car and then, uh, got to start with a, unfortunately it was automatic, but it was a Z 28. We're going to drive LT one. I had a little cul -de -sac at the end of my road and I would just do donuts, man. And that thing, that was a just power slide, you know, and just get that thing sideways, uh, always was obsessed with that.
moments.why: His drifting started with donuts in an automatic Camaro Z28 in a cul-de-sac.

moments.quote: it was cool because I actually got my first job at a Nissan dealership. So at 15, I started working at a Nissan dealership, um, and worked there for a few years and that was, uh, 2005. So that was at the time, like the Z just came out in no three. So I got to just drool over through the Z work on them. I was like the guy that would, uh, if you bought a new car, I'd go like, fill it up with gas and drop it off the detail and then like, bring it to them so they can basically give you the new car. So I got to like drive all these cool cars, like ETR, some used cars. Um, so yeah, man, I just kind of worked really hard and I was able to work out a deal for a three, three 50 Z, uh, brand new when I was like 17 years old. Nice. Yeah. So it was just like a, um, uh, employee discount financed it.
moments.why: He worked at a Nissan dealer from age 15 and bought a brand new 350Z at 17.

moments.quote: And I'm a big Corvette guy. I think the best looking car out there, of course. Uh, and, uh, we jumped into that platform at the time where there was like zero aftermarket support, uh, around COVID. And there was, uh, just a bunch of cars for sale at the time because I think there was no aftermarket support. So it wasn't really a hyped up car at the time. So we got to essentially Trey. I traded like a three of the Z and a G 35 and, uh, was able to trade, um, directly for the Corvette. So I have a crazy story on that. I literally think like we're, I got into the Corvette, like sub $2 ,000.
moments.why: He traded a 350Z and a G35 for the Corvette and paid under 2,000 dollars on top.

moments.quote: And so once we built the car, uh, both the car, it was essentially a stock motor with angle kit and the right arms and parts and going out there and swinging, uh, at clutch triggers. And I'm sure you remember, man, that was when it went over to fetuses over at freedom factory. It's just like unlimited. You can run a, you know, three 15, whatever, you know, Ron would do bro and whatever, uh, so I was out there with the 400 horsepower car. I'm going up against, you know, fully built pro one guys. Uh, but I loved it, man. Like I loved the whole process of learning, um, and just, you know, growing at in the competitive drifting scene. I remember just like still going to those events and like, we're going to be on the podium, like still having that mindset, like right out the gate. And then just getting completely smashed by, you know, a thousand horsepower. Like I remember going to, I want to again, it's like Jonathan near and his crazy car. And he just dored me. Like I just, and I couldn't keep up with him and dored me. I never called my wife after. And I was just like, man, just like bomb. She's like, what do you expect?
moments.why: His first comps were a 400 hp Corvette against fully built pro cars, and he got smashed.

moments.quote: And so in 24, we went out there swinging, um, and just dealt with, um, not so much mechanical, uh, just like. Just issues with other drivers. Honestly, like we got hit a ton the first year and we just had, um, just things break that kind of put us out of that top spot. I think that first year we ended up at like, um, like a fifth or a sixth position. So, um, wasn't the best. Um, and then coming into 25, um, the car was dialed. Everything was ready to go. We did. There wasn't like a learning curve or anything like that. Um, and we just kind of set out to make it happen in 25. And it was a super successful year. I think, uh, we ended up podium, like, I think three out of the four rounds, uh, multiple first places. I think we won it by like 200 points.
moments.why: After a rough first Pro-Am year he won USDC in 2025 by about 200 points.

moments.quote: Evan over at lead foot and Achilles, uh, their, their buddies of mine. So I've always helped out anytime I can with them. They reached out originally and they, me and Dan and, and Shulman went out there and did some initial testing for them. So Achilles always calling my line. He's like, what do you think about this? What do you think about that? Evan, his son has been doing amazing on to the promotion side of things. Socials have been out there. That's all him. So shout out to Evan. So yeah, they've been kind of giving me the sneak peeks of what they got, you know, going, so I'm excited. Uh, and now we just need about two more of those throughout the state. And it will be in a good spot.
moments.why: He helped test Lead Foot, a new Florida drift venue, and wants two more in the state.

moments.quote: So I know there's a lot, you know, that they have tried. Um, and I've even seen, um, you know, a mock -up of the actual, they want to build a track behind the skit pad, like an actual roof course. I've seen the plans for that for six, seven years, you know, like, yeah, I know it's there, um, and it's just kind of on them and just having all those stars align and of course the, the track owner being on board on that side. Cause I know they make a ton of money on the drag side. So it's just kind of like, what do we need to invest into the drifting? If we don't see the return at the end of the day, uh, again, it's just, you know, as a business owner, I see all the sides, but the drifter in me is just like, let's just fricking pave that thing.
moments.why: He has seen plans for a road course behind the OSW skid pad for six or seven years.

moments.quote: We've been super fortunate just with the amount of practice in the rain. And that's why like anytime in FD, when it ran, I was go, because I know, especially on these banks and these old rules, man, like I love driving in the rain on the old, like it's not a bank done deal. I'm like out there doing the rain dance, you know, like I'm like, what let it rain. Especially because we dealt with a ton of motor issues and power delivery issues this year. I was like, man, if it rains, we all got a thousand horsepower.
moments.why: With engine trouble all year, rain was his equalizer in FD.

moments.quote: It was, it was rough for us and it was like in my mind, like I'm like watching everything, you know, years prior, I'm like, man, why do all these guys come to the FD have all these changes and look like a fish out of water? I'm like, once we get our license, we will not do that. And then of course we get our license. I'm like, all right guys, we need more power. So we go and make all these upgrades to the motor. And then unfortunately it's just, this isn't the right recipe. And it's like, this is what we got to use. Um, and it's like, I literally just all year, man, I'm like, I wish we just kind of kept this setup we had in program. I just thought I was a little underpowered. Um, and unfortunately it's just the setup we went with this year. It just didn't give us the sauce we needed.
moments.why: He swore he would not change everything for FD, then chased power and lost his setup.

moments.quote: And it's just like going back to his crew, man. It's just, I remember watching just in Atlanta, the first round, like my crew was there with him and they had, um, impact and went into the wall. And, um, with Gucci, I think, I just remember them pulling the car apart, like it coming in and the work they did in five minutes. And one of my crew guys just looked at me and he goes, we got a lot of work to do just because of how dialed and like things come in. They don't even say anything. Like every single person knows their job. Every single person knows this is the tool. This is the size I need. Um, and that just takes years, man, of practice and really kind of going through the right setup, um, and just really learning everything in and out of the car and it just, it comes with experience. Um, and I was definitely humbled by just all of that.
moments.why: Seeing Matt Field's crew rebuild after a wall hit in five minutes humbled his team.

moments.quote: FDs, uh, it's, it's insane how, it's insane how different it is compared to even a pro -am series, right? Like, I think this year, um, there was only one round that we actually had more than four laps in practice. Wow. So yeah, I think Atlanta around one, we had two laps in practice. The first lap, the car over -rotated and went into the wall, uh, same wall. Matt hit my very first practice lap in FD. That's exactly how it went. So didn't start off so great. Uh, and then, um, it just kind of, you know, went downhill from there to be honest. It just, uh, it's just, uh, yeah, it was just rough this year. So we, uh, and you know, a lot of people are like, Oh, this is your rookie year. You got to expect that. But for me and my team, like we have very high expectations, right? And we were like, all right, this is where we're going to be. This is what we need. Uh, and we're going to execute and be on that podium.
moments.why: His first ever FD practice lap ended in the same wall Matt Field hit.

moments.quote: Like in pro -am I could literally, we have probably two, maybe three sessions, an hour and a half each. So like three, four and a half hours of practice. Um, and here, like I said, man, you're, you're lucky to get three, four laps. Um, with how many drivers are in prospect and site someone was in the wall and they're in, you lose 20 minutes. Um, and so, uh, I think Atlanta, yeah, we got two laps. Um, Connecticut, I think we got two laps. Um, Indy, we got, I think five laps. Um, and that was the only, um, event that we actually had success with the motor set up and just everything. And then last round, I think we got three laps.
moments.why: Pro-Am gave him hours of practice, FD PROSPEC gave him two to five laps.

moments.quote: and then as soon as I like knew, okay, we're probably gonna get our license, I'm gonna be like, I want to reach out and I want to work with someone next year. I really want to learn, of course, like I'm going to go ahead and learn from the Corvette master, right? And so, uh, just reaching out to him and I'm like, brother, like I see what you're doing on the marketing side. Um, and I think I can help you. And it's just very strict. That's a bold statement, right? Yeah. And I'm just like, listen, man, like this is what I essentially can offer you. And this is what we can do. Um, and I think that, you know, at first he was like, well, how are you different than the 60 other media guys that come out to every single event? And I'm like, brother, like we're going to go a completely different route for you.
moments.why: He pitched the Corvette master on marketing to earn his help in FD.

moments.quote: And I really kind of, uh, was taken back by how much he actually invested into me and my program. Like, it wasn't just like, cool, you're going to do this. We're going to help you out. It was very much so him checking me on me. Like, did you do this, do that? Like, what's the alignment currently? Um, and then when he came out to Orlando, he spent a bunch of time with me and the team going over the car, dialing in the car. So just going above and beyond. Uh, and it didn't feel like a transactional. It was very much so a personal, um, relationship with him. And, um, yeah, I just thank him for all the support, um, the guidance this year and just staying on me and just really exposing a lot of things that like changes that we need to make to be successful. Um, and he, he's tough on me, man. Like he'll tell me the truth. He'll be like, yeah, this, this isn't it. Or like, you got to do this. And then his mom and dad as well, like, yeah, they are, I, I'm so thankful for the relationship with them as well. Like his mom's like, yeah, you need to do this. You need to do that. She's like, these are the type of hero cards you need. Like all this and the merch.
moments.why: Matt Field and his parents mentored him hard, down to hero cards and merch.

moments.quote: You don't understand like the fire that's been lit under my butt matter for next year to do everything that we possibly can. Like the car was back from Vegas in two days. Like they already pulled the car apart already on plan a of like trying to get into the best spot for next year. So like we can test next month. Like we're not, we're not playing like we're like, all right, this is what's needed. These are the partners that we're focusing on. This is a setup we want to focus on and doing things like practicing five minute, you know, calls and changes. Oh, that's a good one. Man, like that's a good one. All that stuff. So we can pull up next year and we're like, yep, we're going to be a top contender and that's it.
moments.why: The car was torn down two days after Vegas, testing next month, aiming for top contender.

moments.quote: I remember telling my dad, Hey, I'm moving to LA and he's like, yeah, good luck with that. And I had $500 in my name, you know, and that was a jumping in to the scene. I think that Russian roulette video, I literally worked. It was an 18 hour a day and I got a $20 gas stipend. Damn. So it's like, people don't understand like the industry and like what you truly have to do to like get in the right position. Uh, and like, that's just an example, man. Like that was a short film and there, they probably had a budget of $5 ,000 total for this thing. And there was mainly all volunteers and it was like my first, uh, you know, I guess putting my toes in the water or whatever you want to call it, uh, on an actual film set.
moments.why: He moved to LA with 500 dollars and worked 18 hour days for a 20 dollar gas stipend.

moments.quote: So cool facts. The, I, when I moved out to LA, I worked for a DP at the time, director of photography, and he was the one that shot all Lincoln parks music videos. That's crazy. Small world. And Michael Jackson, he did a bunch of Mike, Michael Jackson music videos. And so I was basically his assistant. He was like, yeah, this is what you need to do to be successful. And I just remember like looking at his reels and like he worked for huge hubby Gucci, a Maserati Bentley, like all these high end brands. Um, and just seeing like his journey, but yeah, he did all Lincoln parks. That's cool videos and stuff like that. So yeah, shout out to Ross Richardson.
moments.why: His first LA mentor was the DP behind Linkin Park and Michael Jackson videos.

moments.quote: I think all it truly comes down to it was like, of course we want to always elevate. Right. Like we all want to come out next year, like swinging. Um, of course it just comes down to. Funding and getting the right partners involved. Um, and so we're definitely in that process. Like again, we just want to elevate it and put the right people in place, but there's some pretty big, uh, things brewing on the interclip side, uh, along with formula drift that, uh, uh, we can't say just yet, but things, things are bubbling, so we're really, we're really excited. Um, hopefully these things really kind of go through. Um, and we want to grow, like the whole point of the series is like a drive to survive type of series.
moments.why: He hints at something big brewing between Interclip and Formula DRIFT.

moments.quote: I think drifting needs it. I think it will help with, um, the fan base. I think F1 got a huge, uh, uptick in, you know, fans after all that came out. Cause then the day then you can be, you can relate to the drivers, you know, and you can see what they're going and dealing with. Um, you can see how they handle these situations. Um, and I think it's super powerful. It's just, we are, uh, we're slowly starting to see, you know, kind of a wave of some guys trying it as well. Right. The longer form type of content. And that was such a big thing where we had a pitch to Matt and Brandon of like, it's going to be long form. It's not going to be like the snappy stuff, but like the viewer count and the watch time like speaks for itself. Like these are 40 minute videos and people are watching, you know, 98 % of the video. Like it's, it's insane. And so kind of like that really speaks for itself. It shows us, Hey, there is a demand.
moments.why: Their 40 minute videos keep viewers for 98 percent of the runtime.

moments.quote: Matt's Matt's insane though. That man can riff off. And I'm like, Oh, just like, you know, partner bits of like, say this, say that. Like we just like tell him, and then he just like just nails it. I'm like, yeah, that's just like, and that comes with the experience, right? And all the years of doing that and being camera ready. Uh, but yeah, these interviews take a long time and just like the whole editing process, uh, the amount of time that Loxie will take for these edits. Uh, it's like a full week essentially. Um, and so it just takes a lot, um, from everything down to sound design for each and every clip and, and, and sinking of, uh, 12 cameras, you know, like everything is like time coded and go across the board so we can see what camera at what time, so we know we can pull it.
moments.why: Matt Field nails every line, but each edit takes a week with 12 synced cameras.

moments.quote: Uh, but they are, um, cooking up an episode that covers around two, three, and four of mine. So we have, of course, yeah. So we have the first round out in Atlanta, just kind of showcasing like how rough that round was, uh, and then we're going to have just like one big, uh, episode for myself here coming out in the next few weeks. So, uh, we're cranking out Matt's last round video and that should be going live this week and the weekend. So obviously on the podium. Uh, so we're super excited about that. Uh, I was just like, man, we got to get a win because no one wants to watch the same thing, dude blow the door up every round. And it's just like, we'll be back next round.
moments.why: An Interclip episode on his rounds two to four is coming, plus Matt Field's podium video.

moments.quote: Like we get to record all Matt's like teams comms. And so like, man, the editing on that has got to be wild. Oh my God. It's just, it's just funny. Cause like Jacob and Loxley, like they have, uh, you know, uh, ear whatever so they can hear everything just from their comms. Then we're recording that to basically and time coding that as well. And so we have all that, but man, like the stuff that they say and like how they just operate and flow throughout the day, it's like, I, you can listen to that stuff alone and it'd be like the best content ever. So it's just kind of going that extra level and, and, and that's the stuff that you're not going to hear or see anywhere else. Yeah. And so like having that and being like, this is what chow his spotters saying to him in this moment and stuff like that. Like he can be so brutal to Matt, like, but it's, it's, it works for them.
moments.why: They record Matt Field's team radio, and the spotter can be brutal.

moments.quote: Brother on top of that, I also, we had our second kid in between rounds two and three. Yeah. So I was told, I was like asked a ton of the end of the year, like, how are you going to operate your business, FD program, new kid, all the interclip stuff? Like, I'm just like, I'm the type of guy that's just like loaded up, you know, I might get through it. And I think just the motivation that keeps me going is that I'm able to do it. And I want to prove that I can do it and being able to like overcome whatever tasks is in front of me. I'm big on just mental performance, spend a lot of time and money on, on that stuff to get my mindset right. Um, and it trickles from, you know, business all the way down to FD. And it just, I walk in like, that's it. Like you, if you see me on grid, like I'm not the guy that's like out of my car, shooting the shit with every other driver right before we go on practice. Like I'm locked into my seat. I have everything, you know, I have my cool suit on. I have my earbuds in like I'm locked in and looking forward.
moments.why: His second kid arrived between rounds two and three of his rookie FD year.

moments.quote: Yeah, I think sleep is number one, but also I work with a sports psychologist. Oh, nice. So having my mindset, but more so keeping me level minded and like saying certain things to myself when I need to say things, then even to practice breathing, like that was something where I was never taught how to properly breathe. And I was like, it sounds so woo woo and dumb, but it is one of the most life -changing things you can learn.
moments.why: He works with a sports psychologist and calls learning to breathe life-changing.

moments.quote: Um, visualizing, like I visualize over and over and over again, the run, I visualize me winning the battle. I visualize the guy pointing to me, you got the win, like that type of stuff. And so when I do get in that position, I feel like I've already been there. And so all the, like I had no nerves whatsoever all year. And like, it's because I mentally prepared myself to be in that position, to be in that seat, especially with the SIM helping out of like literally seeing everything and knowing, okay, this is where I'm going to be.
moments.why: He visualizes winning every battle so he had zero nerves as an FD rookie.

moments.quote: Um, I mean, for us this year, just kind of finishing at the bottom, I think next year, like at a minimum, man, it's like, we have to be a top 10 competitive. Um, of course, like I'm going to tell you, like, we're going to be on the box every single round. Um, but like the realistic goals is just to have a car that is working a hundred percent, um, and just myself being comfortable behind the wheel with all the changes we made this year. Like I felt like I was driving someone else's car for the first three rounds. Like I'm just like, dude, this doesn't feel right. Um, you know, this isn't, this isn't my car. I don't feel comfortable. I'm not going to be able to perform at the level I can.
moments.why: After finishing at the bottom, his minimum goal for next year is top 10.

moments.quote: Uh, I'm just bummed out about how it all kind of panned out, but, uh, yeah, like the one round we, we had essentially like a car, uh, when we made it's top 16 and then, uh, Jerry Johnson took us out and top 16, which was, it was a pretty close battle, but it was a good battle. Everyone was like, Oh, I don't, I didn't know you could drive like that. I'm like, and so I think that's just a really big bummer, man. Like just like people truly think like what we did this year is like the level of my driving, which is like, yeah, embarrassing. Um, you know, but it's just like, again, man, it lights a fire in my butt. Like I cannot wait to get back out there.
moments.why: His one working weekend ended in Top 16 and people finally saw what he can do.

moments.quote: I, I will have my G out there for black Friday. I have a G sedan with the one J in it. And we just, uh, put a four door cage with four bucket seats. Oh, sick. Okay. Yeah. So I really wanted to build a car to like be able to just give ride alongs and, you know, share the experience of drifting. Uh, also give back to the partners that's kind of helped on the build. Um, and so yeah, we're going to be, uh, bringing that car out for black Friday. So super excited about that. And it should be a good time.
moments.why: He built a 1JZ G sedan with a four door cage to give ride-alongs at Black Friday.
